evidence.topic: Real subprocess intent, outcome, streams and durability
evidence.assessment: New caller and only the needed unchanged A34 operational primitives reviewed statically; no A35 serial-case native receipt was supplied to this reviewer.
evidence.details: The A35 loop calls execute_case synchronously with exactly one explicitly allowed taskset CPU and one-thread BLAS environment; there is no executor or second concurrent worker. The reused worker durably publishes the exact launch intent before Popen, uses a new process session, records spawn, writes raw stdout/stderr to exclusive files, observes the real child with wait4, and publishes actual exit/cost plus stream bindings. Both streams are flushed/fsynced before outcome publication. save_json persists file data and its containing directory; make_directory recursively persists newly created ancestors and their entries. A35 read_exit explicitly accepts the reused A34-named outcome schema and requires matching record/argv/CPU, actual integer exit 0, and no termination/error; it authenticates both raw streams before load_case. Reuse applies the same operational receipt gate before scientific admission.

evidence.topic: Signals, reaping, finite grants, failed/unknown costs and no retry
evidence.assessment: Static operational paths inspected; not executed by the reviewer.
evidence.details: SIGINT/SIGTERM set the shared stop event. The worker checks stop, batch deadline and case timeout, kills the child process group when required, waits for a real terminal status, and reaps on the exception path. Pending records are not launched after stop/deadline. Consume accounts for the durable outcome even on failure, replaces missing/nonfinite/negative measurements with unknown rather than zero, and marks failed-generation physical-action count unknown. Costs exclude reused-generation work explicitly. A worker failure or scientific rejection unwinds the synchronous loop; there is no automatic in-invocation retry or recovery of temporary action arrays. A later invocation is a new explicit attempt and only committed compatible generations are reusable.
